speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the specific nature of the bleeding you are experiencing, such as how often you get nosebleeds or if you notice any easy bruising on your skin. Additionally, have you experienced excessive bleeding after minor cuts or dental work?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any family members with bleeding disorders, and does the child have any joint swelling or deep muscle pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_platelet_count_and_bleeding_time. REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time_and_Partial_Thromboplastin_Time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal); Prothrombin_Time (PT) 12 seconds (normal), Partial_Thromboplastin_Time (aPTT) 30 seconds (normal). Special_Test (ELISA_Binding_Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lab results show normal platelet counts and coagulation times, but the ELISA test confirms a deficiency in GpIIb/IIIa receptors on the platelet surface. This finding is pathognomonic for Glanzmann's thrombasthenia.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
